subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add a public core scheduling contract for prime-derived cadence and deterministic phase jitter on heartbeat and cron `every`, and what backward-compatible default/API shape should own it?
rationale: Source inspection shows the remaining gap is real, but the fix defines new scheduler semantics, config keys, CLI flags, protocol fields, and persisted cron behavior that automation should not choose without product intent.

options.title: Design one narrow core contract
options.body: Add a default-compatible heartbeat/cron interval scheduling model with explicit ownership of defaults, persisted shape, CLI/docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Limit the scope to cron every jitter
options.body: Treat heartbeat as already solved by shipped stable phases and design only an interval-job jitter/phase field for cron `every`.

options.title: Decline prime and keep existing phase behavior
options.body: Close the product direction by documenting existing heartbeat phase spreading and cron-expression stagger as the supported anti-herd tools.

recommendation.title: Design one narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Add a default-compatible heartbeat/cron interval scheduling model with explicit ownership of defaults, persisted shape, CLI/docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across cron CLI/API ergonomics and schedule identity surfaces that would carry the new public contract.
